bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on capital-market and economic conditions — Management states the capital market industry is mainly dependent on the economic growth of the country and is further affected by international policies of foreign governments and any change in the international business environment.
- Concentration of assets in associate and group-concern companies — The company's investments and loans are made in associate and group-concern companies, and management says it is making efforts to realise those investments and loans for better deployment, so recovery depends on a small set of related entities rather than third parties.
- Strategic and commercial risk — Flagged in the MD&A risk list as being taken care of by the Risk Management Committee with reporting to the Board on a need basis.
- Regulatory compliance risk — Management states the regulatory environment has resulted in increased regulatory scrutiny that has raised the minimum standards to be maintained by the company, and that regulatory requirements can at times be challenging.
- Financial risk including interest-rate movements and liquidity — Disclosed as including exposure to movements in interest rates, with the company maintaining sufficient liquidity so it can meet financial commitments on due dates and is not forced to obtain funding on unfavourable terms. The sentence is cut off mid-disclosure in the bundle.
- Macro and geopolitical factors — Geopolitical tensions, rising crude oil prices, rising US bond yields and scams in the banking sector are named as factors affecting the country during the year under review.
- Sensitivity of industrial growth to external factors — Management describes industrial growth as very sensitive and dependent on many social, financial, economical or political factors as well as natural climatic conditions in the country.
- Internal control and internal audit adequacy — The company relies on internal controls commensurate with its size and operations and notes that the statutory requirement of a compulsory internal auditor for listed companies will further strengthen its internal control measures.

business.body: Amit Securities Limited was incorporated as a public limited company on 17 June 1992 with the Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra. Per its Corporate Information note, the company is primarily engaged in the trading of aluminium utensils and investments in mutual funds, shares and securities. It reports two segments - trading of goods and carrying investments, and trading of shares and advances - and sources its aluminium utensils from associate concern Mittal Udyog (Indore) Pvt. Ltd.

sk.overview: India's digital financial services and NBFC-led retail lending sector serves a large, young, credit-underpenetrated mass market. Formalization (GST, JAM/India Stack, eKYC), rising smartphone/internet penetration and low data costs are enabling tech-led NBFCs and fintechs to underwrite and serve borrowers that conventional banks have historically underserved, particularly in unsecured personal loans and loan-against-property.
sk.schemes: Digital India|JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) / India Stack|eKYC / DigiLocker|OCEN / ONDC|PMJDY financial inclusion|Udyam / MSME formalization
sk.structure: NBFCs hold ~18-19% of systemic credit and ~23% of the combined personal-loans and LAP market (FY2025), accounting for 25% of personal loans and 21% of LAP. Tech-led NBFCs/fintechs (Kissht, Moneyview, KreditBee, Fibe) capture share from cautious conventional lenders via digital-first, AI/ML …
